brief.headline: Close the 13.6% price gap to our best Dextrose rate and move toward the ₹42.95/kg India export benchmark.

priceAsk.summary: Reduce Dextrose to ₹66.48/KG or below, matching our best price from Sayaji Industries Limited.
priceAsk.target: ₹66.48/KG on Dextrose Anhydrous IP and all Dextrose grades; potential annual saving ₹14.26 L
priceAsk.basis: We currently pay them ₹75.51/KG — 13.6% above our best price of ₹66.48/KG. India export unit value sits at ₹42.95/kg, proving headroom exists.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold current 30 Days After Receipt terms; no extension.

brief.financialLeverage: Universal Starch reports revenue of ₹514.62 Cr with a 3.7% net margin and 7.4% EBITDA margin — thin by any standard. Debt-to-equity of 0.73x is manageable but not fortress-strong. They carry a C health score (51/100). Our ₹59.65 L spend is just 0.12% of their revenue, so standalone leverage is negligible. However, they are growing at 21.4% per year and hunger for volume, which gives us an opening to trade committed tonnage for a lower unit price. Push firmly on price — they need the growth — but watch for quality or delivery slip if margins compress further.

evidence.point: We pay 13.6% more than our best Dextrose supplier
Closing the gap saves us ₹14.26 L annually
India export benchmark for Dextrose is far lower, signalling market headroom
Their net margin is razor-thin at 3.7%, limiting their ability to absorb cost shocks but also proving price discipline is possible
We represent only 0.12% of their ₹514.62 Cr revenue, so we need competitive tension to move them
They are growing top-line at 21.4% per year and will value volume commitments

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch and polyol maker; established dextrose/sorbitol supplier — a drop-in alternate with C health.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist growing capacity in starch and dextrose; B health score.

alternates.name: Roquette India Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Indian arm of global starch major; pharma-grade dextrose and excipients with premium reliability.

risks: At 0.12% of their revenue we lack unilateral clout — credibly threaten to shift volume to Sayaji, Gulshan, or Sanstar.
Their 3.7% net margin is already wafer-thin; aggressive price cuts may trigger quality or lead-time compromises — build quality KPIs into any new contract.
No credit rating or interest-coverage data in hand; if liquidity tightens they may push for earlier payment — do not budge on the 30-day terms.
Growing at 21.4% means capacity may be stretched; confirm lead times and minimum-order commitments before locking in volume.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but at ₹75.51 per kilo we're paying 13.6% over our best Dextrose price — let's close that gap and talk about a volume commitment in return.
